classification.difficultyReason: Infer the missing overlap from the class total, then select and combine the correct regions for exclusive or, intersection and inclusive or before dividing by 80.

content.prompt: The Venn diagram below shows the number of students speaking French, Italian, both, or neither in a classroom of 80 students.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3, two-circle diagram below the opening sentence
spec.description: Two overlapping, unshaded circles inside a rectangle. Italian is on the left and French is on the right.
spec.mathematics: Italian only is 15, French only is 35 and neither is 21. The universal set contains 80 students.
spec.answerVisibility: The intersection remains blank for the student to complete.

children.prompt: By first finding the missing information in the Venn diagram above, write down the probability that a randomly chosen student

answer.worked:
The 21 students outside both circles speak neither language.

$$P(\text{neither})=\frac{21}{80}$$

spec.description: Completed Italian and French Venn diagram.
spec.mathematics: The four regions contain 15, 9, 35 and 21 students respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: The intersection count of 9 appears only in the solution figure.

children.label: b
children.prompt: speaks Italian or French only, but not both.

answer.worked:
Use the two regions outside the overlap.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one})&=\frac{15+35}{80}\\P(\text{exactly one})&=\frac{5}{8}\end{align*}$$

Count everyone inside either circle, including the overlap.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{French or Italian})&=\frac{15+9+35}{80}\\P(\text{French or Italian})&=\frac{59}{80}\end{align*}$$
